findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - closing a Forge pull request after the installer job is removed.
The deleted windows-installers job remains required by forge.toml:8. src/forge/close.py:463 passes that list to checks.wait, and src/forge/checks.py:250 reports an absent required check as not reported. Consequently, close cannot finish even when every remaining job passes. Complete the coordinator's settings update alongside this deletion.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - the nightly full suite receives an Ubuntu 24.04 runner.
Setting FORGE_STARTER_LIVE enables the tests, but full-suite never selects Node 24 as starter-smoke does. tests/test_starter_tree.py:165 skips both live starter stacks unless Node reports v24; tests/test_libs_layout.py:94 likewise skips live lint coverage. The [Ubuntu 24.04 image](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/actions/runner-images/main/images/ubuntu/Ubuntu2404-Readme.md) defaults to Node 22 and still serves ubuntu-latest during the [current rollout](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/14748). Those nightly runs therefore skip the promised live coverage. Select Node 24 and ensure Corepack is available before running the suite.

stop.reason: The owner chose one more round: confirm the required checks and set Node 24 for the nightly starter tests.

why: Pull requests print the net-line count in two places: the net-lines job in .github/workflows/forge-next.yml and the pull request size step in .github/workflows/forge.yml. The Windows installer test runs in its own windows-installers job and again in the Windows platform groups, but only for pull requests that change non-test code. Removing the job also drops the only Windows check on test-only pull requests that touch no platform test. Starter smoke's live tests skip unless FORGE_STARTER_LIVE is set, and the nightly full run in forge.yml does not set it, so moving them to nightly needs that variable set too.
